lecture_beats.subject: tensor equations, invariant zero, and the scalar-gradient control case
moving coordinate bases and failure of the ordinary vector derivative
connection correction, sign convention, and one correction per tensor index
radial polar field, curvilinear components, and metric compatibility
Levi--Civita connection, Christoffel formula, and upper-index derivative
normal coordinates, local flatness, curvature, and exterior differentiation
parameterized curves, tangent vectors, and covariant differentiation along a path
geodesic equation, Newtonian comparison, and curvature preview

resolved_source_issues.issue: The first lower-index correction is written with a plus sign on the board.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The temporary coefficient is named C and identified as minus Gamma before the standard Levi--Civita convention is adopted.

resolved_source_issues.issue: Several free and dummy indices are corrected during the live rank-two derivation.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter preserves the corrections and writes one correctly indexed connection term for each tensor slot.

resolved_source_issues.issue: Metric compatibility and the connection formula can inherit the earlier temporary sign.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: Both formulas are normalized to the standard torsion-free, metric-compatible convention.

resolved_source_issues.issue: Vanishing Christoffel symbols at one point can be misread as global flatness.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter distinguishes normal coordinates at one point from zero curvature on a neighborhood.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The spoken polar-coordinate metric component is misstated.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter uses the correct varying component g theta theta equals r squared.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The exterior derivative is compared informally with curl.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter states the three-dimensional Euclidean identification and Hodge-dual qualification.

resolved_source_issues.issue: The parameter condition behind the geodesic equation is implicit.
resolved_source_issues.resolution: The chapter identifies an affine parameter and explains why arc length or proper time supplies it here.

uncertain_sources.note: The live temporary coefficient is retained as C equals minus Gamma so the visible board and the standard convention remain distinguishable.
The Newtonian comparison is presented as the lecture's forward bridge rather than a completed weak-field derivation.
